content.text: ## Story S8: Orchestrator invocation contract in COMMIT-WORKFLOW.md + Value validation canary
### Description

**What**: Document the orchestrator's invocation contract for the new primitive in COMMIT-WORKFLOW.md: invoke `start` via `Bash(run_in_background: true)` → `bash_id`, drain progress via `BashOutput(bash_id)` for streaming only, poll `<state_dir>/done` for completion, read `<state_dir>/exit-code` as the authoritative result. Include an explicit "do not treat BashOutput return-empty as completion" note. Separately, execute the Value validation SC: on a canary worktree, run one representative test-gate cycle under both the legacy `test-batched` path and the new primitive on the same commit, record tool-call counts and total tokens consumed in the epic closure comment, assert the new path uses ≤3 tool calls and reduces tokens by ≥50%. INSTALL.md is also updated here with a pointer to the new test-run primitive.

**Why**: The orchestrator contract is the agent-facing API of the new primitive. Without clear documentation, every caller risks misusing `BashOutput` as a completion signal (one of the critical scenarios from brainstorm). The Value validation canary is the SC that gates epic closure on measured improvement.
**Scope**:
- IN: COMMIT-WORKFLOW.md contract section, INSTALL.md pointer, canary measurement script + fixture, closure comment with numbers
- OUT: CLAUDE.md full architecture update (S9 doc refresh)
### Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, COMMIT-WORKFLOW.md includes an "Orchestrator invocation contract" section describing `run_in_background` dispatch, `BashOutput` for progress-only, `done` marker polling, and `exit-code` read, with an explicit "do not treat BashOutput return-empty as completion" note

← Satisfies: "Orchestrator invocation contract — documented in COMMIT-WORKFLOW.md: the orchestrator invokes test-run start via Bash(run_in_background: true) ... Explicit 'do not treat BashOutput return-empty as completion' note"

- When this story is complete, a canary worktree runs one representative test-gate cycle under (a) the legacy path and (b) the new primitive on the same commit; both tool-call count and total tokens from dispatch to verdict are recorded in the epic closure comment

← Satisfies: "before closing the epic, a canary worktree runs one representative test-gate cycle under (a) the legacy test-batched path and (b) the new background primitive, on the same commit. The epic closure comment records both tool-call counts and total tokens consumed"
- When this story is complete, the closure comment documents that the new path completed in ≤3 tool calls AND reduced tokens by ≥50% vs the legacy path on the same suite

← Satisfies: "Acceptance: the new path completes in ≤3 tool calls (1 dispatch + ≤2 drains) and reduces tokens by ≥50% vs the legacy path on the same suite. Failure to meet either threshold blocks epic closure pending approach revision"
- When this story is complete, unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic
### Considerations

- [Testing] The specific canary workload (suite or file-edit trigger) must be pinned and recorded alongside the numbers so future regression tests are comparable — reviewer-flagged minor refinement from brainstorm
- [Reliability] This is the SC that can block epic closure; run it before S9 docs update so docs reflect measured outcomes

content.text: ## Context

The existing kudos system (Epics 3e9b-afee and 71df-5bd8) includes 5 triggers that silently skip on non-Python stacks. T7 uses Python ast.NodeVisitor. T9 uses ruff (Python-only). T12 uses Python-anchored regexes. T13 and T4 use Python ast.dump() subtree hashing. Ruby and JavaScript developers receive zero kudos from these 5 triggers. This epic replaces them with polyglot equivalents so kudos fires across all supported stacks.
## Success Criteria
- T7 uses lizard -ENS instead of Python ast.NodeVisitor; supports Python, JS/TS, Ruby, Java; 30s timeout; --exclude for test dirs; when lizard absent: TRIGGER_SKIPPED signal
- T9 reads commands.lint (from Epic B); when absent: TRIGGER_SKIPPED; when present, fires on zero-violation result
- T12 uses line-start-anchored regexes covering Python, JS/TS, Ruby, Java syntax for commented-out code detection
- T13 and T4 use jscpd (JSON reporter to temp dir, 30s timeout, exit code parsing); when jscpd absent: TRIGGER_SKIPPED
- All five triggers emit machine-readable TRIGGER_SKIPPED signal conforming to the signal format established by Kudos Epic 2 (71df-5bd8); no shared library imported from Kudos Epic 2
## Closure Checks
## Operational Constraints (Architecture-vs-Evidence Audit Remediation, 2026-05-18)
### State Lifecycle Owner Block (Probe-3 remediation)
| Variable | CREATE | UPDATE | CONSUME | RETIRE |

| `commands.lint` (dso-config.conf, written by Epic B / 3818-310d) | `/dso:onboarding` writes per detected stack at project setup | Operator edit; re-onboarding APPENDS new stacks, never overwrites existing | T9 trigger reads at evaluation time | N/A — persistent per-stack config; key removed only if stack itself is removed from project |

| `TRIGGER_SKIPPED` signal format (shared with Kudos Epic 2) | Each polyglot trigger emits this format when its tool is absent (per the spec) | Format is versioned via `schema_version` field; breaking changes bump version + migration | Kudos Epic 2's aggregator consumes and surfaces in retro | N/A — wire-format protocol; retired only via formal schema version bump with consumer migration |
Verification (in-session, at sprint Phase I):
- `grep -E '^commands\.lint=' .claude/dso-config.conf` shows the key with a sensible default OR an empty value that's documented as "stack-specific, set by /dso:onboarding".
- `grep -nE 'TRIGGER_SKIPPED|schema_version' <plugin-kudos-trigger-scripts>` confirms the signal format is emitted with explicit version field.

- Validation: sprint acceptance test environment has lizard and jscpd installed; test matrix covers all 5 triggers before/after on non-Python files; before: no kudos for Ruby file; after: kudos fires for quality improvement; Kudos Epic 1 must be present in CI or dispatch_kudos_trigger() mocked
## Dependencies
- Epic B (3818-310d): T9 reads commands.lint; without Epic B, T9 always emits TRIGGER_SKIPPED
- Kudos Epic 1 (3e9b-afee): T13 and T7 call the kudos dispatch function delivered by Kudos Epic 1; runtime blocking dependency (blocks relationship in ticket system)
- Kudos Epic 2 (71df-5bd8): runtime consumer dependency — Epic C conforms to TRIGGER_SKIPPED signal format so the existing event emitter can handle it
## Approach

Replace each of the 5 Python-specific trigger implementations with polyglot equivalents: lizard for AST-based nesting analysis (T7), jscpd for duplicate block detection (T13/T4), language-neutral regexes for commented-out code (T12), and commands.lint config key for lint-clean detection (T9). All triggers emit TRIGGER_SKIPPED when required tooling or config is absent.
## Research Findings
- External integration (lizard): -ENS flags emit nesting/size metrics; supports Python, JS/TS, Ruby, Java, C/C++; `command -v lizard` absence detection; 30s subprocess timeout required

- External integration (jscpd): JSON reporter to temp dir (`--reporters json --output <dir>`); exit code 0 = no duplicates, 1 = duplicates found; parse via `cat <dir>/jscpd-report.json` (file-based, not stdout); 30s subprocess timeout required
- Dependency (commands.lint from Epic B 3818-310d): polyglot lint config key; absent → TRIGGER_SKIPPED; present → fires on zero-violation exit
- Signal format (TRIGGER_SKIPPED): conforms to Kudos Epic 2 (71df-5bd8) signal format independently — schema duplicated, not imported, to preserve epic independence
## Scenario Analysis
- lizard binary absent in CI (high, deployment): T7 voids awards; TRIGGER_SKIPPED signal emitted per Kudos Epic 2 schema; document or accept skip as designed
- jscpd binary absent in CI (high, deployment): T13/T4 void awards; TRIGGER_SKIPPED signal emitted per Kudos Epic 2 schema; document or accept skip as designed
- commands.lint key absent from dso-config.conf (high, configuration): T9 always emits TRIGGER_SKIPPED; onboarding/architect-foundation must populate this key per detected stack
- lizard/jscpd subprocess exceeds 30s timeout (medium, runtime): kill and treat as TRIGGER_SKIPPED; explicit timeout handling required with SIGKILL after grace period

- TRIGGER_SKIPPED signal format drift from Kudos Epic 2 schema (high, integration): format validated independently per epic; schema change in Epic 2 silently breaks Epic C signals — add schema conformance test in this epic
- T12 regex false-positive on language-specific block comments (medium, correctness): Python `"""`, Ruby `=begin/=end`, JS `/** */` need language-aware anchors beyond simple line-start matching
## Risk Register (from preplanning)
- Testing (03d4-062a, 988f-933e): External binaries need subprocess mocking
- Maintainability (all story): TRIGGER_SKIPPED signal format must conform to Kudos Epic 2 schema independently
- Reliability (a1f9-2e8b): dispatch_kudos_trigger() from Kudos Epic 1 must be present or mocked in acceptance env
### Planning Intelligence Log
- **Web research (Step 2.6)**: triggered
- Bright-line conditions that fired: external integration (lizard, jscpd CLIs), dependency on another epic (Epic B commands.lint key, Kudos Epic 2 signal schema)
- **Scenario analysis (Step 2.75)**: triggered
- Scenarios surviving blue team filter: 6
- **Practitioner-requested additional cycles**: none
- **Follow-on scrutiny (Step 0)**: not triggered
- **Feasibility resolution (Step 2.5)**: not triggered
- **LLM-instruction signal (Step 5)**: not triggered
- **Scale context (Step 0)**: small scale (default) — per-commit polyglot triggers; not volume-sensitive

content.text: ## Story C: Test-gate recording scripts consume `commands.test_runner` (replace hardcoded pytest)
### Description

**What**: Update the test-gate recording script (hardcoded `python3 -m pytest`) and the test-gate exemption script (hardcoded `python3 -m pytest "$NODE_ID"`) to read `commands.test_runner` and invoke it with the target test path. This is the behavioral payoff — Ruby and JS projects get real test-gate signal from this story.

**Why**: Today `.rb` and `.js`/`.ts` files produce no test-gate signal because the recording script skips the hardcoded pytest call for non-Python files. Ruby and JS projects appear to pass the gate while their tests are never actually run.
**Scope**:
- IN: both hardcoded pytest call sites replaced with config-key reads, exit-code propagation preserved (0=pass, non-zero=fail), centrality-aware tier mapping unchanged
- OUT: per-file gate (Story E), reinstall-hooks.sh precondition change (Story D), config-absent warning path (covered by library helper if needed)
### Done Definitions
- When this story is complete, neither script contains a hardcoded `python3 -m pytest` invocation

← Satisfies: "record-test-status.sh routes .rb, .js, .ts files to commands.test_runner instead of hardcoded python3/pytest" + "record-test-exemption.sh uses commands.test_runner instead of hardcoded python3 -m pytest"
- When this story is complete, recording on a `.rb` source file in a Ruby-detected project invokes `$commands.test_runner` and captures its exit code as the test result
← Satisfies: "record-test-status.sh routes .rb, .js, .ts files to commands.test_runner"
- When this story is complete, the recording script emits an actionable `[DSO WARN]` when `commands.test_runner` is missing at gate execution time and skips (does not silently pass)
← Satisfies: epic Scenario Analysis "commands.test_runner absent at gate execution time"
### Considerations
- [Testing] Mock `commands.test_runner` in unit tests; do NOT invoke real pytest/rspec/jest
- [Reliability] Exit code 0/non-zero contract identical across pytest/RSpec/Jest (confirmed in epic Research Findings); no per-runner special-casing required
- [Testing] Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic

content.text: ## Description

**What**: Replace the Python-specific ast.NodeVisitor implementation of T7 with a lizard-based approach using `lizard -ENS` to measure cognitive complexity (nesting depth) across all supported stacks. Emit TRIGGER_SKIPPED when lizard is not on PATH.

**Why**: T7 today can only measure nesting depth in Python files. Ruby and JavaScript developers who reduce deeply-nested code receive zero kudos. Lizard supports Python, JS/TS, Ruby, and Java, making it the natural polyglot replacement.
**Scope**:

- IN: `lizard -ENS` subprocess with 30s timeout; `--exclude` flag for test directories; compare before/after nesting depth from git diff; TRIGGER_SKIPPED when `lizard` not on PATH; TRIGGER_SKIPPED on non-zero lizard exit; award kudos when nesting depth decreases
- OUT: Installing lizard in CI (covered by SC6 / Story E); T9, T12, T13, T4
## Done Definitions
- When this story is complete, T7 fires and awards kudos on a JS/TS file where nesting depth decreased (measured by lizard), and does NOT fire on a file where nesting depth increased or stayed flat
← Satisfies: "T7 uses lizard -ENS instead of Python ast.NodeVisitor; supports Python, JS/TS, Ruby, Java"
- When this story is complete, T7 emits a machine-readable TRIGGER_SKIPPED signal (not an exception) when `lizard` is not found on PATH
← Satisfies: "when lizard absent: TRIGGER_SKIPPED signal"
- When this story is complete, T7 does not hang — subprocess call enforces 30s timeout; timeout → TRIGGER_SKIPPED
← Satisfies: "30s timeout"
- When this story is complete, test directories are excluded from lizard analysis (`--exclude` passed for dirs matching test/spec patterns)
← Satisfies: "--exclude for test dirs"
- When this story is complete, the TRIGGER_SKIPPED signal fields conform to Kudos Epic 2 (71df-5bd8) schema; no shared library imported from Kudos Epic 2
← Satisfies: "All five triggers emit machine-readable TRIGGER_SKIPPED signal"

- When this story is complete, unit tests written and passing for: PATH-absent case (TRIGGER_SKIPPED), timeout case (TRIGGER_SKIPPED), nesting-decrease case (award), nesting-flat/increase case (no award)
## Considerations
- [Testing] Mock `subprocess.run` (or equivalent) to avoid requiring lizard binary in test environment; test PATH-absent, timeout, zero-exit-code-with-no-decrease, and award-path cases
- [Maintainability] TRIGGER_SKIPPED signal format: reference Kudos Epic 2 (71df-5bd8) for the required field schema; implement independently (no import from Kudos Epic 2 modules)
- [Reliability] dispatch_kudos_trigger() from Kudos Epic 1 (3e9b-afee) must be mocked in unit tests
- [Reliability] Timeout handling: subprocess timeout=30 must be caught and converted to TRIGGER_SKIPPED, not propagated as an exception
## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.

- Any failure blocks sprint closure with diagnostic showing both outputs

- [Integration] Gate must short-circuit (PASS with note) when loader is globally disabled (flag-off mode); distinct from per-epic activation check — prevents false-fail when epic's tickets are in scope but loader is globally off for the sprint
